title: Detach-to-Primitive: Zoom, Wrap, Text Checks, Rebuild Menu
summary: Three confirmed bugs from an independent audit of the detach-to-primitive kit, each reproduced, fixed and mutation-verified, plus the right-click "Rebuild" menu Zach asked for, wired onto tldraw's own stock context menu.
intro: The previous lane's own report claimed 0px offsets on card and port-ring geometry, all real. A Fable audit dug past that and found two things it missed and one thing its own test suite could not have caught: (F1) the kit never read the camera's zoom, so a detach anywhere but z=1 baked the zoom straight into the model; (F2) a wrapping label detached to one overhanging line; (F3) the suite's ONLY text-placement check was a port ring's centre, and a comment falsely claimed that stood in for checking the text itself.

This lane fixed all three, added the right-click "Rebuild" menu item Zach asked for (composed onto tldraw's own stock context menu, not a replacement for it), and mutation-verified every fix by reverting it and watching the exact reported symptom reproduce.
changes: apps/storybook-basics/src/detach/stockShapes.ts — boxRelativeTo/textBoxRelativeTo now read editor.getZoomLevel() themselves instead of taking a scale = 1 default (F1); textAtDom gained a wrap branch that lets a multi-line label wrap at its own measured width instead of forcing one overhanging line (F2)

apps/storybook-basics/src/detach/definitions/{block,port}.ts — the four call sites now pass editor through to the fixed helpers; port.ts's stale "24px default" comment corrected to 18px (F5, the code already read the computed style)

apps/storybook-basics/src/hosts/tldrawHost.tsx — one additive prop, components?: TLComponents, merged over the host's own { OnTheCanvas }, plus an exported useTldrawHostScene() hook so a component mounted through that prop can still reach {scene, onSceneChange}

apps/storybook-basics/src/detach/rebuildContextMenu.tsx — new: composes tldraw's own DefaultContextMenu/DefaultContextMenuContent with one conditional "Rebuild" group, gated on selectedRebuildableIds(editor).length > 0

apps/storybook-basics/src/stories/DetachToPrimitive.stories.tsx — per-string text-node ink-box assertions (F3) replacing the false "the ring IS the text check" comment; two new permanent gallery rows (wrapping header, long single-line header); a new ZoomInvariance story (z=0.5/1/2); a new RebuildMenuStates story (both menu states, driven at z=2) plus a capture-only variant; a hidden-tab guard on the shared nextPaint() helper
docs/ALGORITHM-PROVENANCE.md — three new src/detach rows citing why F1/F2/the menu have no donor precedent (the donor's pure layout function has no DOM, camera or context-menu concept at all)
findings: F1 (zoom), mutation-verified: reverting the zoom division reproduces the exact reported symptom — a 220×140 card detaches to 440×280 at z=2, and to 110×70 at z=0.5. Fixed: identical 220×140 card / 22×22 rings at z=0.5, 1 and 2 — see the zoom table below

F2 (wrap), mutation-verified: reverting the wrap branch reproduces the exact reported symptom — the 3-line live header (measured ink 162.6×59) detaches to one 393px-wide line, overhanging a 220px card by ~115px on the left alone. Fixed: the detached label wraps to 166.4×56 — inside the card, not one line

F3 (text placement), mutation-verified two ways: an injected 8px text-offset bug is CAUGHT by the new per-string ink-box checks (dx=8 > the 6px floor) and is INVISIBLE to the old card+ring-only checks (same bug, same suite with the new checks disabled, passes clean) — direct proof the old "the ring is the text check" comment was false

The audit's own drift projection did not materialize: a genuinely long (~163px) single-line header measured 2–3.6px of before/after drift, not the projected ~6–7px per edge — the chosen tolerance (max(6, ceil(width×4.5%))) passes it honestly without needing to be loosened

Rebuild menu, both states + a real click: absent on a live (non-detached) selection, present after detaching, and clicking it through the REAL context menu (not a direct function call) rebuilds the live component — driven at z=2 throughout, so this is also F1's integration proof through the actual entry point a user would use

Full baseline held and grew cleanly: tsc clean; unit project unchanged at 40 files / 744 tests; storybook project 62 files / 271 tests (was 62/268 — +3 tests, all mine), every number below is this run's own console.table/JSON output, not retyped from memory

sections.heading: F1 — camera zoom baked into the model
sections.html:
The bug: boxRelativeTo/textBoxRelativeTo convert a screen-space getBoundingClientRect() into model units by dividing by the camera zoom — except they never did: the parameter defaulted to scale = 1 and all four call sites omitted it, so nothing in the kit ever read editor.getZoomLevel(). A screen rect already includes the zoom, so dividing by 1 instead of the real zoom bakes the zoom straight into the model.

The fix: both functions now read editor.getZoomLevel() themselves — the fix lives at the SOURCE, not at four call sites that would each have to remember to pass a number by hand (exactly the mistake that caused this).

Mutation-tested: reverting the read back to a hardcoded 1 reproduces the exact symptom — z=0.5 shape #0 (rectangle) w vs z=1: expected 110 to be less than or equal to 1, i.e. the card measured HALF size at half zoom, exactly the inverse-of-zoom bug shape. Restoring the fix returns every shape to the SAME 220×140/22×22 geometry regardless of zoom (see the table below, and the captures — note the visual capture needed a wider stage AND a held camera to actually show the difference; see the caption).

images.title: Before — z=2 detaches to ~2x the model (BUG)
images.caption: Reintroduced the bug for this capture (reverted, screenshotted, restored). z=0.5 (left): the card and both rings shrink to a sliver — the model was halved along with the halved zoom. z=2 (right): the header alone overflows the whole 960px stage — the model was doubled along with the doubled zoom. z=1 (middle) looks fine, because dividing by the bugged constant 1 happens to equal dividing by the real zoom exactly when zoom IS 1 — which is exactly why a bench fixed at z=1 forever would never have caught this.

images.title: After — identical model geometry at every zoom (FIXED)
images.caption: Same story, same code path, only the fix restored. z=0.5, z=1 and z=2 all show the SAME proportioned card and ports — bigger on screen at higher zoom (correct: that is what zooming in looks like), never a different MODEL size. The zoom-percent readout in each toolbar (50% / 100% / 200%) is tldraw's own camera; the shapes underneath are what "model geometry" means here.

sections.heading: F2 — a wrapping label detached to one overhanging line
sections.html:
The bug: textAtDom floored a detached label's width at Math.max(box.w, tldrawWidth), where tldrawWidth is tldraw's own SINGLE-LINE measure of the whole string — the right safety floor for a label that fits on one line (so tldraw's different font metrics can never wrap it early), and exactly backwards for a label that already wraps: it forces the WHOLE string onto one line no matter how tall the live DOM's own measured ink box was.

The fix: derive a line count from the live DOM's measured ink-box height (Math.round(box.h / lineHeight)); when it is more than 1, hand tldraw the DOM's own measured WIDTH instead of the single-line floor, so it wraps at roughly the same width the live component did.

Mutation-tested: reverting the wrap branch reproduces the exact reported symptom — wrapping-header detached header must not overhang the card (F2): expected 392.8 to be less than or equal to 226, matching the bug report's own "one 393px-wide line" almost to the pixel. Restoring the fix returns the detached label to 166.4px wide (inside the 220px card) and 56px tall (still ~3 lines, matching the live header's 59px) — see the captures.

sections.heading: F3 — per-string text placement, and the false comment it replaces
sections.html:
What was there before: the ONLY thing standing in for "is the text placed correctly" was the port ring's own centre — a geometry check on a dot, not on any text node. The story's own comment claimed this WAS the text-placement check Zach asked an adversarial loop over ("I don't like how when you convert there are these pixel offsets"). That claim was false, and F3 replaces it with real per-string checks.

The fix: Range.getBoundingClientRect() on the actual header/label text nodes — the same technique stockShapes.ts's own textBoxRelativeTo uses internally to BUILD the primitives — measured before→detached and before→rebuilt, for the header and every port label, on every gallery row.

Proven necessary, not just added: an injected 8px horizontal text-placement bug (moving textAtDom's x by a flat +8px, leaving card and ring geometry untouched) is CAUGHT immediately by the new checks (dx: expected 8 to be less than or equal to 6) and is INVISIBLE to the old suite — the exact same bug, with F3's checks disabled to simulate the pre-fix suite, passes clean. That is direct proof the old comment was wrong, not an assumption.

Tolerance, chosen deliberately: a flat 6px (this repo's existing geometry tolerance) passes today's short strings but is the wrong SHAPE of bound — the residual is font-substitution advance mismatch (tldraw's bundled tldraw_sans vs. this app's system-sans stack), a PERCENTAGE of a string's width, split in half by centering. The chosen tolerance is max(6px, ceil(width × 4.5%)) — floored at the existing bar for short strings, scaling for long ones so a real placement bug on a long string still fails loudly.

The audit's own projection, tested and NOT confirmed: the audit projected a ~150px single-line label would drift ~6–7px per edge, past a flat 6px cap. A genuine ~163px single-line header ("Long single-line header (F3 tolerance)" row, added specifically to test this) measured 2–3.6px of drift — well inside even the OLD flat 6px tolerance. The projection does not hold at this string length; whether it holds further out is unmeasured.

sections.heading: The right-click "Rebuild" menu
sections.html:
Zach's own words: "When you do rebuild, it detects if there is rebuild info in the group you selected and displays the option in the right click menu." The previous lane flagged this as blocked ("no context-menu override hook in this tldraw version") — true of TLUiOverrides, wrong about tldraw: the context menu is a replaceable COMPONENT SLOT (TLUiComponents.ContextMenu), verified directly against tldraw 5.3.2's own .d.ts mid-lane.

Composed rather than replaced: RebuildContextMenu renders tldraw's own DefaultContextMenu wrapping DefaultContextMenuContent (every stock item — Edit, Arrange, Reorder, Cut/Copy/Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Copy as, Export as, Select all) plus one conditional "Rebuild" group. Wired through a new components prop on TldrawHost, additive, mirroring the existing onEditorReady seam.

Both states verified with a real right-click (fireEvent.contextMenu, not a direct function call): absent on a live, not-yet-detached selection; present after detaching; clicking it rebuilds the live component. Both mutation-tested (forced the group to always/never render — each caught by the corresponding assertion). Driven at z=2 throughout — this is also F1's integration proof through the real entry point a user would actually use, not just the dedicated ZoomInvariance bench.
